message.content:
Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city.
They loved the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and most of all they loved houses.
The nicely laid out stone walls formed shelters from the weather yet connected the earth with the stories from every family.
They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their own staff.
The first wall taught them that stone liked to be placed slowly.
The second wall taught them that patience made the mortar stronger.
The third wall taught them that a door should welcome both rain and memory.
The fourth wall taught them that a roof could hold the sound of distant songs.
The fifth wall taught them that a floor could carry a family's quiet hopes.
The sixth wall taught them that a window could frame the morning sky.
The seventh wall taught them that a garden needed a place to grow.
The eighth wall taught them that a bridge should connect two longing hearts.
The ninth wall taught them that a hillside could hold a small secret.
The tenth wall taught them that a tree could share its shade with neighbors.
The eleventh wall taught them that a river could bless a new doorstep.
The twelfth wall taught them that a lamp could turn night into a story.
The thirteenth wall taught them that a cup could hold a toast of thanks.
The fourteenth wall taught them that a table could gather many voices.
The fifteenth wall taught them that a chair could hold a tired friend.
The sixteenth wall taught them that a bell could call the city to rest.
The seventeenth wall taught them that a road could carry laughter home.
The eighteenth wall taught them that a field could dream after the harvest.
The nineteenth wall taught them that a spring could give a city its quiet heart.
The spring softly remembered the bridge the wall the roof the door the window the floor the garden the tree the branch the root the seed the rain the wind the bird the song spotty as a mark of joy.
